settings.purpose: Final assessment of two-stock Heston basket pricing methods, neural and classical. No training, tuning or model selection may use these cases or their references.
settings.model: Each stock has its own Heston variance (v0, kappa, theta, xi) and leverage rho_i = corr(dW_i, dZ_i). The variance drivers Z have correlation C (vol_correlation); W_i = rho_i Z_i + sqrt(1 - rho_i^2) Y_i with Y independent of Z and correlation P, so the stock correlation is R = (rho rho') o C + (rbar rbar') o P (src/heston_basket/model.py). The Feller condition is not imposed.
settings.conventions: Strike fixed at 100. Time in years; rates, dividend yields and variances are decimals. Vega is d/dv0 per stock; the Heston-parameter and correlation sensitivities are per unit change; theta is calendar time per year; rho per unit rate.

domain_constraints.weights: On the simplex with every weight >= 0.1, uniform: w = 0.1 + 0.8 * D with D ~ Dirichlet(1, 1).
domain_constraints.correlation: The variance correlation C and the residual correlation P are drawn independently, each with entries uniform on its range and the smallest eigenvalue >= 0.05 (rejection); the stock correlation R follows from the leverages, so R is always valid. The R range above is the attainable range, used to scale network inputs.

sampling.latin_hypercube: scipy.stats.qmc.LatinHypercube(d=17, seed=seed + split offset): columns 1-16 scale to the box parameters, column 17 is a uniform whose spacings (0, u, 1) are a uniform Dirichlet(1, 1) draw for the weights.
sampling.correlation_stream: numpy.random.Generator(PCG64(seed + 100 + split offset)); per case, C's entries then P's entries uniform on their ranges in pair order, each matrix redrawn until its smallest eigenvalue >= 0.05.
sampling.options: Calls and puts alternate within each split, starting with a call.

short_maturity.reason: remaining life below the training domain; tau = 0.005 + 0.045 * (the tau column's uniform)

extrapolation.reason: one parameter outside the training domain
extrapolation.stock_rotation: Single-stock parameters move stock 1 and then stock 2 across the 2 cases of each value.
extrapolation.notes: A weight value goes to the affected stock and the other weight is 1 minus it. A correlation value fixes the pair's entry of C or of P (pair 1-2); R follows from the leverages as for every case.

cases.name: near_black_scholes_call
cases.note: close to the two-stock Black-Scholes basket

reference.method: Conditional QE simulation (src/heston_basket/engine.py): Andersen's QE scheme with martingale correction for each stock's variance, the variance normals correlated by C; given the variance paths the log returns are Gaussian and the basket option is the conditional estimator of src/pricing (one factor in closed form, the residual factor sampled). Replicated scrambled-Sobol RQMC with a Brownian bridge; analytic conditional Deltas and Gammas; central common-random-number bumps for theta, vega and the parameter and correlation sensitivities; rho = -tau V + tau sum_i S_i dV/dS_i.
reference.acceptance: Climb the points per replicate until the price standard error is at most the target (currency units, strike 100); keep the first level that meets it. A case still above the target at the last level keeps that level and is flagged; no case is replaced.
reference.seeds: Production run seed = protocol seed + 10000 + case index; cross-check run seed = protocol seed + 20000 + case index.

cross_checks.independent_run: A second estimate at the accepted level with its own seed; z = (second - reference) / sqrt(se_1^2 + se_2^2) per quantity; |z| > 5 is flagged for a look.
cross_checks.time_step: The production seed with dt doubled (1/32): z = (coarse - reference) / sqrt(se_1^2 + se_2^2) measures the QE time-step bias (the doubled step has about twice the reference's bias).
cross_checks.bump_halving: bump_scale 0.5 at the accepted level with the production seed (common random numbers); maximum relative change of the bumped quantities.
cross_checks.relative_floors: Relative differences divide by max(|reference|, floor) with floor 1e-7 for Gammas and 1e-4 otherwise.
cross_checks.use: Recorded only; never used to change a reference.
cross_checks.points: Every cross-check runs at min(accepted points, 16384) per replicate; the z-scores use both runs' standard errors. The bump-halving change is measured against the production seed at the same points.

separation.metric: For a test case and a development contract, the largest over parameters of |difference| / domain width (moneyness, tau, rate, dividends, the Heston parameters, weights and the entries of C and R; widths from the training domain). The reported separation is the minimum over all pairs.
separation.duplicates: No test case may equal a development contract (same option and all contract fields within 1e-9).

rules: Train, tune and select models only on data generated with other seeds; never on these cases or references.
Development and training data must use seeds other than 20261018 and its offsets and must keep a positive minimum distance from every test case under the separation metric; report that distance.
Before evaluating any model on these cases, freeze its checkpoint hash, settings and the evaluation protocol.
Report every method on every split; do not drop cases after seeing results.
Every reference carries a standard error and a time-step bias check; report method errors next to them, and do not read differences below about three reference standard errors as differences.
Once any method is evaluated here, the cases are observed; later model changes need a new test set.
settings.laptop_edition: Laptop edition (18 Oct 2026, for the CSE Tech Day poster): the build was cut to fit a laptop before anything was sealed. Points per replicate stop at 16,384 (65,536 for the lab PC) and the cross-checks run at 4,096.
